exact_statement: For every finite uniform Boolean restriction stopping tree with a single uniform terminal FEI constant C0, Boolean semi-separated children at each internal node give H(f)<=max(C0,12)I(f); monotone tribe-separated nodes give H(f)<=max(C0,14)I(f). Every GMP delta-tribes function H+(G-H)AND_u, where H is disjoint tribes on m bits and G is OR of those bits and one new bit, satisfies H(f)<=23I(f), with disjoint-tribes terminals paid by the reconstructed 14-rate theorem. These are conservative corrections of the source consequences, not optimality or priority claims.
hypotheses: Uniform measure on {-1,1}^n; f sign-valued; Shannon entropy in bits
Physical finite restriction tree; no repeated query along a path; node reach weights 2^-depth
A common dimension-independent C0 for all terminal functions in the class
Semi-separated children: pq and pr with sign-valued p,q,r on pairwise disjoint coordinate sets
Tribe-separated node: monotone children h and max(h,k) with h,k on disjoint coordinates
Delta-tribes: shared AND width u>=1; disjoint positive widths for H; m=0 allowed with H=-1; G includes one fresh bit
proof_source: GMP26 v2 Proposition 6.1 and source class structure
